children: At the end of June, promoter entities hold 27.14 per cent of Billionbrains Garage Ventures, while public shareholders own 71.75 per cent
Shares of Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of Groww, fell nearly 3 per cent on Wednesday after a large block deal involving around Rs 1,999 crore worth of shares changed hands.

Groww shares traded 3.66 per cent lower at Rs 192 apiece on the NSE during morning trade. Around 10.41 crore shares, representing 1.69 per cent of the company’s equity, were transacted through block deals at Rs 192 per share.
The identities of the buyers and sellers were not immediately disclosed. The transaction took place at a price close to the reported floor price of Rs 191.45 per share.

The base offer was reportedly for up to 1.6 per cent of Billionbrains Garage Ventures’ outstanding shares, with the shares involved subject to a 30-day lock-in on further sales. The large transaction has put the stock under pressure as investors assess the potential for further stake sales by existing shareholders.

At the end of June, promoter entities held 27.14 per cent of Billionbrains Garage Ventures, while public shareholders owned 71.75 per cent. Employee Trust holdings accounted for the remaining 1.11 per cent.
Among public shareholders, Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1 held 15.68 per cent and Sequoia Capital Global Growth Fund III - US/India Annex Fund held 1.46 per cent.
The block transaction comes after several sizeable stake transactions involving Groww this year, adding to investor focus on the company’s shareholder exits and the supply of shares in the market.
The selling pressure comes despite a positive assessment from Jefferies, which on Tuesday described Groww as a way to participate in India’s broader equity-market growth.
The brokerage noted that futures and options account for nearly 55 per cent of Groww’s topline and said a resolution to the ongoing Closing Auction Session (CAS) issue could benefit the company.

Jefferies expects Groww to have multiple drivers of earnings growth, including its core broking business, margin trading facility and wealth management initiatives. It estimates a 30 per cent compound annual growth rate in profit after tax between FY26 and FY29, supported by around 18 per cent growth in broking revenue and an expansion in margins.
The brokerage also expects Groww’s planned addition of US stocks to its platform by the end of FY27 to potentially increase its FY28 earnings estimates by 5-9 per cent.

Jefferies has retained its Buy rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 240 and included Groww among its financial outperformers, a list of companies it expects to deliver operating profit growth of at least 25 per cent annually over the next three years.

The contrasting signals of a large block transaction and continued positive brokerage expectations have put the focus on whether the current selling represents an isolated stake sale or the beginning of further supply from existing investors.
